newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat calls killing of Israeli women 'barbaric'.
newsitem.headline: Arafat calls killing of Israeli women 'barbaric'.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat on Sunday described as "a barbaric, shameful act" the stabbing to death of two Israeli women whose bodies were found in the West Bank.
He said in self-ruled Jericho that Israeli and Palestinian security officers had met on Saturday to discuss the issue.

"This is a barbaric, shameful, unethical act. Whoever did it must be ashamed and it is completely unacceptable by any side," Arafat told reporters after meeting former cabinet minister Yossi Beilin, a candidate to head the opposition Labour party.

Israeli police said on Saturday they had asked Palestinian police to help investigate the killings. The women's bodies were found by hikers on Friday in the Wadi Qelt nature reserve in the West Bank, about five km (three miles) from Jericho.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu told army radio that Israel had yet to identify the assailants. Israeli police said they were investigating whether the killers were Palestinian guerrillas.

"It appears to be a murder against a nationalist background but we cannot say as yet with certainty," Netanyahu said. He said he hoped "there will be real cooperation" with Arafat's Palestinian Authority.

The women were identified as Hagit Zavitsky of the Jewish settlement Kfar Adumim in the West Bank between Jerusalem and Jericho, and Liat Kastiel of the town of Holon near Tel Aviv. Both were 23 years old.
